_README: HELD-OUT retrieval cases -- a check that the Phase 2 retrieval method was not
fitted to the 15 cases in phase2_testset.json.
Written 2026-09-26 AFTER the method was chosen on phase2_testset.json and
BEFORE it was ever run on these cases; it was scored once, with the method
frozen, and the result recorded in stuff/docs/phase2_retrieval.md whatever it was.
Do not tune retrieval against this file -- the moment you do, it stops being
held out and a new one has to be written.
Same provenance rules as phase2_testset.json: the queries are SYNTHETIC facts
drafted by Claude; every `relevant` section was checked against the real
ingested text of that section before being listed, none written from memory;
no statutory text is stored here (corpus_from loads it). The legal judgement
of which sections the facts disclose is Claude's, not a lawyer's.

cases.query: The accused attended a family function at the complainant's house as a guest. After he left, a gold chain was found missing from the dressing table in the bedroom. Two days later he pledged the same chain at a pawn shop.

The accused told the complainant he could get her son a government job through his contacts, took three lakh rupees from her for processing fees, handed over an appointment letter that turned out to be fake, and then stopped answering her calls.
In a quarrel over a parking space the accused slapped the complainant and punched him in the face. The doctor recorded a swollen lip and bruises on the cheek and described the injuries as simple.

The accused, a truck operator, was engaged to carry two hundred bags of cement from the factory to the buyer's warehouse. He delivered only one hundred and twenty bags and sold the remaining eighty to a hardware shop on the way.

Two brothers came to the complainant's house carrying sticks after telling the neighbours they would settle scores with him. One stood in the doorway to stop him escaping while the other struck him repeatedly, fracturing his forearm.
The accused worked as a domestic help in the complainant's flat. Over several weeks she took cash and a mobile phone from her employer's cupboard; the phone was traced to her through its IMEI number.
A man on foot ran up behind the complainant while she waited at a bus stop, pulled the gold chain from her neck in one quick movement and ran off into a side lane.

The accused sold the complainant a used car for four lakh rupees, concealing that it was hypothecated to a bank and showing him a no-objection certificate that the bank had never issued. The bank later repossessed the car.
During a dispute over farmland the accused hit the complainant on the head with a brick. The complainant suffered a skull fracture and remained in hospital for twenty-five days.

The accused was the cashier of a private company and was handed the day's cash collections to deposit in the company's bank account. Instead of depositing the money he used it to repay his personal loans.
